title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 191 (Payment to director for loss of office, etc., in connection with transfer of undertaking, property or shares)

content.overview: Section 191 restricts payments to a director by way of compensation for loss of office, or as consideration for retirement from office, or in connection with such loss or retirement, in connection with the transfer of the whole or any part of any undertaking or property of the company, or the transfer of shares resulting from certain offers. Particulars must be disclosed to members and the payment approved by a resolution of the company. Unapproved payments are held in trust for the company or for persons who have sold their shares, as the section provides. The section does not authorise a payment that also breaches sections 197 or 202.
content.glance: Payment to director for loss of office/retirement linked to transfer of undertaking, property or shares needs disclosure of particulars and company resolution; unapproved payment held in trust; does not override ss. 197/202 limits.
content.study: No director of a company shall, in connection with the transfer of the whole or any part of any undertaking or property of the company, receive any payment by way of compensation for loss of office, or as consideration for retirement from office, or in connection with such loss or retirement from any person, unless particulars with respect to the payment proposed to be made by such person have been disclosed to the members of the company and the proposal has been approved by the company in general meeting. Similar disclosure and approval rules apply to payments in connection with the transfer of shares resulting from an offer made to the general body of shareholders, or from certain other offers specified in the section. Where a payment is made in contravention, the amount received is deemed to have been received in trust for the company or for the persons who have sold their shares, as applicable. Current-law framing: identify the payment and the connected transfer; require disclosure of particulars and company resolution; apply the trust consequence on breach; check that ss. 197 and 202 are not independently breached.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Compensation for loss of office or consideration for retirement, paid in connection with transfer of undertaking/property or with specified share transfers.

sections.heading: Disclosure and Approval
sections.body: Particulars of the proposed payment must be disclosed to members and the proposal approved by the company in general meeting.

sections.heading: Trust Consequence
sections.body: Unapproved payments are held in trust for the company or for selling shareholders, as the section states.

sections.heading: Other Limits
sections.body: Section 191 does not authorise a payment that also breaches the remuneration or compensation limits in ss. 197 and 202.

provisions.title: Payment to director for loss of office, etc., in connection with transfer of undertaking, property or shares

examples.title: Payment on sale of undertaking
examples.body: On a sale of the company’s main undertaking, a director is to receive a large sum as compensation for loss of office from the purchaser. Section 191 requires disclosure of particulars to members and approval by the company in general meeting.

examples.title: Unapproved payment held in trust
examples.body: A director receives a loss-of-office payment connected with a share transfer offer without the disclosure and approval required by s. 191. The amount is held in trust for the selling shareholders (or the company, as the section applies).

hypotheticals.question: Does member approval under s. 191 override the overall remuneration ceiling in s. 197?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 191 is a disclosure-and-approval rule for a specific class of payments. It does not authorise a payment that independently breaches section 197 or section 202.

distinctions.title: Loss-of-office payment on transfer (s. 191) vs compensation for loss of office (s. 202)
distinctions.left: Payments linked to transfer of undertaking/property/shares; disclosure and GM approval
distinctions.right: General rules on compensation for loss of office of MD/WTD/manager

misconceptions.trap: Any Board-approved farewell payment to a director is valid without member disclosure.
misconceptions.correction: Where the payment is compensation for loss of office or retirement consideration connected with a transfer of undertaking, property or specified share transfers, s. 191 requires member disclosure and approval.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 191 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify payment and connected transfer. II. Require disclosure and GM approval. III. Apply trust consequence on breach. IV. Check ss. 197/202. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Payment facts; transfer link; disclosure/approval status; precise relief.

examTips: Transfer-linked loss-of-office payments need disclosure + GM approval.
